If we add on all the square of a number's every digit, it end up with result 1, we call this number is a happy number. It's easy to end the loop by detecting the emerge of 1. But how can we know when to end the endless loop without knowing whether 1 will appear? Here is the maths prove behind it: For one digit numbers, the max is 9, its square sum is 81, far bigger than 9. For two digit numbers, the max is 99, its square sum is 81+81=162, slightly bigger than 99.
